title: Compact remainder estimate gives coercivity on the kernel complement
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], let $E$ be a Hilbert space, meaning a real inner product space complete for its inner product norm. Let $F,Z$ be real normed vector spaces, with norms satisfying definiteness, the triangle inequality and $\|av\|=|a|\|v\|$. Let $T:E\to F$ and $J:E\to Z$ be bounded linear maps. Assume that $J$ is compact, meaning every bounded sequence $(x_n)$ in $E$ has a subsequence for which $(Jx_n)$ converges in $Z$. Suppose there is $C>0$ such that $\|x\|_E\leq C(\|Tx\|_F+\|Jx\|_Z)$ for all $x\in E$. Put $K=\{x\in E:Tx=0\}$ and $K^\perp=\{v\in E:\langle w,v\rangle=0\text{ for every }w\in K\}$. Then there exists $D>0$ such that $\|v\|_E\leq D\|Tv\|_F$ for every $v\in K^\perp$.

source.place: VI §2 proof of Corollary (2.4)(ii), compactness and norm-estimate argument (2.5), printed p.290; abstract Hilbert-space kernel-complement formulation isolated by NU, with normalized-sequence proof in report.md; WANTED locally, read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: Argue by contradiction. If no $D>0$ works, then for each integer $n\geq1$ choose $x_n\in K^\perp$ with $\|x_n\|>n\|Tx_n\|$. Thus $x_n\ne0$; put $v_n=x_n/\|x_n\|$. Linearity and norm homogeneity give $v_n\in K^\perp$, $\|v_n\|=1$ and $\|Tv_n\|<1/n$. Consequently $Tv_n\to0$.

source.place: VI §2 proof of Corollary (2.4)(ii), printed p.290, compactness/norm-estimate argument (2.5); abstract normalized-sequence proof written by Q98, rather than a numbered assertion of Demailly. PDF absent locally; source pages read online.

proof.text: The sequence $(v_n)$ is bounded since every norm equals $1$. The compactness hypothesis on $J$, with exactly the sequential meaning given in the statement, supplies strictly increasing indices $n_j$ and $z\in Z$ such that $Jv_{n_j}\to z$. Write $u_j=v_{n_j}$; then $\|u_j\|=1$, $u_j\in K^\perp$ and $\|Tu_j\|<1/n_j\to0$, since $n_j\geq j$.

source.place: VI §2 proof of Corollary (2.4)(ii), printed p.290, compactness/norm-estimate argument (2.5); abstract normalized-sequence proof written by Q98, rather than a numbered assertion of Demailly. PDF absent locally; source pages read online.

proof.text: Apply the assumed estimate to $u_i-u_j$ and use linearity and the triangle inequality: $\|u_i-u_j\|\leq C(\|Tu_i\|+\|Tu_j\|+\|Ju_i-z\|+\|Ju_j-z\|)$. Given $\varepsilon>0$, choose $N$ so each of the four terms is less than $\varepsilon/(4C)$ for $i,j\geq N$. This proves that $(u_j)$ is Cauchy in $E$.

source.place: VI §2 proof of Corollary (2.4)(ii), printed p.290, compactness/norm-estimate argument (2.5); abstract normalized-sequence proof written by Q98, rather than a numbered assertion of Demailly. PDF absent locally; source pages read online.

proof.text: Completeness of the Hilbert space $E$ means that this Cauchy sequence has a limit $u\in E$. The reverse triangle inequality $|\|u\|-1|=|\|u\|-\|u_j\||\leq\|u-u_j\|$ gives $\|u\|=1$. Boundedness of $T$ provides $M\geq0$ with $\|Th\|\leq M\|h\|$ for all $h$. Hence $\|Tu\|\leq M\|u-u_j\|+\|Tu_j\|\to0$, so $Tu=0$ and $u\in K$.

source.place: VI §2 proof of Corollary (2.4)(ii), printed p.290, compactness/norm-estimate argument (2.5); abstract normalized-sequence proof written by Q98, rather than a numbered assertion of Demailly. PDF absent locally; source pages read online.

proof.text: For each $j$, the definition of $u_j\in K^\perp$ applied to $u\in K$ gives $\langle u,u_j\rangle=0$. Symmetry and bilinearity of the real inner product therefore yield $\|u_j-u\|^2=\|u_j\|^2-2\langle u,u_j\rangle+\|u\|^2=2$. This contradicts $u_j\to u$, which makes $\|u_j-u\|<1$ eventually. The supposition that every $D>0$ fails is impossible; this proves the required existence of $D>0$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q98-1c83d74ca (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full; this is a 0-new-node S1 split and the statement is unchanged from the NU base. The statement is the standard Peetre/compact-remainder lemma and is true: on a real Hilbert space E, with T, J bounded and J sequentially compact, ‖x‖≤C(‖Tx‖+‖Jx‖) implies ‖v‖≤D‖Tv‖ on (ker T)^⊥. It matches step 4 of lem-sfb-elliptic-sobolev-closed-range (E=H^k, F=L²(H), Z=L²(G), J compact Rellich), so the target is not weakened. Steps 1–5 checked: (1) the negation with D=n gives x_n≠0, and v_n is normalised in K^⊥ with ‖Tv_n‖<1/n; (2) the stated sequential compactness gives Ju_j→z and n_j≥j; (3) the estimate on u_i−u_j gives four terms each <ε/(4C), so the sequence is Cauchy; (4) completeness of E gives u with ‖u‖=1 by the reverse triangle inequality, and Tu=0 by the operator bound, without completeness of F; (5) ⟨u,u_j⟩=0, so ‖u_j−u‖²=2, a contradiction. All steps are a few lines and need no citation (C1/C2 fine; D fine). Small cases: E=0, T injective, T=0 vacuous, J=0 gives D=C; ℓ² with T x=(x_n/n) and J=id shows compactness is needed. Duplicate search with rg -L over the snapshot DAG (subsequence, Peetre, Hilbert, \perp in sfb): only hilbert-orthogonal-projection and the elliptic parents, none a duplicate. I agree with the Mathlib no-match verdicts (Lax–Milgram and the Fredholm/compact-image lemmas are different facts).
